(Shri Manish Yadav - Advocate For The Applicant)
 (Smt. Varsha Singh Thakur - Ga For Respondent/State)
 Order

1. This is the 4th application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.183/2022 registered at Police Station Bagli, District Dewas for the offence under Section 363, 366-A, 376(2)(N), 376 of IPC and Section 5L/6 of POCSO Act.
2. As per the prosecution story, father of the prosecutrix reported that on 3.4.2023 he and his family went to sleep after diner.

When he woke up at 4.00 A.M. in the morning, he did not found prosecutrix in the house, then he searched for the prosecutrix in the surrounding areas and also in friends and relatives, but he did not found the prosecutrix.
He stated that present applicant, who is resident of Bhatkund, comes to his house often and he doubted upon the present applicant that he has taken away the prosecutrix by alluring her.
Upon which, the police registered the aforesaid FIR.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant contended that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this matter.
He is in custody since 18.7.2022.

Prosecutrix (PW-2) including her father (PW-1) and mother (PW-3) 2 MCRC-27141-2024 have been examined before the trial Court and all of them have turned hostile and did not supported the prosecution story in respect of the aforesaid offence.
There is no legal evidence against the applicant.
He is the sole bread earner of his family and permanent resident of District Dewas.
Hence, he prays that applicant be released on bail.

4. Per-contra, learned GA for respondent/State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that prosecutrix was found pregnant and as per the DNA report present applicant is the biological father of the prosecutrix's son.
Applicant is also having criminal antecedents.
Therefore, applicant is not entitled for bail.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

sentences.text: Considered all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by counsel for the parties, nature and gravity of allegation as also the fact that prosecutrix (PW-2) in her statement before the trial Court categorically stated that the present applicant neither abducted her nor committed rape upon her.
Prosecutrix's father (PW-1) and mother (PW-3) also deposed in the same manner.
Prosecutrix has deposed that she was major at the time of incident.
Her parents have also supported her statement by stating that at the time of incident her age was 19 years.
Therefore, in view of the evidence available on record, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
7. Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by the conditions enumerated u/S. 437(3) Cr.P.C.
3 MCRC-27141-2024 C.C. as per rules.
